before: South Carolina premises liability law requires property owners to maintain reasonably safe conditions for visitors, with the highest duty of care owed to invitees such as hotel guests, restaurant patrons, and attraction visitors. Common tourist injuries in Charleston include slip-and-falls, pool accidents, balcony collapses, and foodborne illness. Out-of-state visitors can file claims in South Carolina courts. The modified comparative fault rule bars recovery at 51% or more fault, and the three-year statute of limitations (S.C. Code SS 15-3-530) applies.
